claims.text: The material family is face-centered-cubic Fe-Co-Ni-based high-entropy alloys.
The property targeted for improvement is saturation magnetization.
The primary scientific challenge is an inability to decouple the orbital magnetic moment from the spin magnetic moment.
Strong spin-orbit coupling and crystal-field quenching cause the difficulty in separating orbital and spin moments.
Failure to decouple orbital and spin moments prevents optimization of the total magnetic moment for soft-magnetic applications.
Equiatomic or near-equiatomic fcc Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloys exhibit high saturation magnetization, low magnetic anisotropy, and a quenched orbital moment.
Adding 1-5 at% Ru, Rh, or Os can introduce a strong-spin-orbit-coupling dopant without phase separation or alteration of the fcc structure.
Arc melting followed by annealing at 1100 degrees Celsius for 24 hours under argon is an appropriate synthesis and homogenization route for the proposed alloys.
A heavy dopant will cause local symmetry breaking and modify the d-band electronic structure near the Fermi level.
The dopant-induced electronic changes will lift d-orbital degeneracy and reduce crystal-field quenching of the orbital moment.
The heavy dopant will increase the effective spin-orbit-coupling strength and partially unquench the orbital magnetic moment.
Partial unquenching of the orbital moment will increase the total magnetic moment per atom.
The proposed mechanism may enhance magnetic anisotropy energy.
The proposed changes may yield higher permeability and lower coercivity if magnetic anisotropy remains sufficiently low.
Heavy-element addition will produce a measurable increase in the orbital-to-spin moment ratio detectable by XMCD.
The increased orbital-to-spin moment ratio will cause either a net increase in saturation magnetization or a significant enhancement of magnetic anisotropy while preserving fcc stability.
In standard fcc Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloys, the cubic crystal field nearly fully quenches the orbital moment, so magnetism is dominated solely by spin.
Exceeding the dopant solubility limit could produce secondary sigma or B2 ordered phases.
A sufficiently large lattice-parameter change could induce a transition to a ferromagnetic bcc or nonmagnetic state.
Any orbital-moment benefit may be negated if stronger spin-orbit coupling increases magnetic damping or coercivity.

contradictions.description: Low magnetic anisotropy is presented as a limitation in the initial state, but the mechanism also requires anisotropy to remain low for good soft-magnetic behavior, while the predicted outcome treats a significant anisotropy enhancement as an alternative improvement.

The predicted outcome permits enhanced anisotropy as an alternative to increased saturation magnetization, whereas the falsification rule rejects cases in which orbital moment increases but saturation magnetization decreases, even if anisotropy is significantly enhanced.
